messages.content: Write a recap post about what a team learned at an industry conference. Around 250 words.

Draft below (~245 words). It passes the repo's own `slopwatch` gate clean.

---

**What we brought back from SREcon**

Five of us went. We came back arguing about one slide.

The talks were fine, and a few were better than that. The postmortem on the April control-plane outage earned the flight on its own — the speaker spent twenty minutes on the two fixes that failed before she got to the one that worked. Most conference postmortems are victory laps. That one wasn't.

The rest of it happened in hallways. Three separate teams, none of whom knew each other, told us the same story: they had ripped out their staging environment. Not scaled it down. Removed it, and moved the budget into progressive rollouts and faster rollback. Same reason every time — staging drifted from prod within weeks and handed everyone false confidence.

We have opinions about that. Marcus thinks it's survivorship bias from shops with deploy tooling we don't have. Priya thinks he's defending a system he built. They might both be right.

Two things we're actually changing. First, we're going to time our rollbacks. Nobody here can tell you how long ours takes, which is embarrassing for a team that says "blast radius" as often as we do. Second, our incident reviews will include the attempts that failed. Cheap to do, and judging by that outage talk, it's the part people remember.

Notes are in the shared doc. Ask us about the vendor floor sometime — that's a different post.

---

output:
**What we brought back from SREcon**

Five of us flew out. We came home still arguing about one slide.

The talks were fine, a couple better than that. The postmortem on the April control-plane outage paid for the tickets by itself — the speaker gave twenty minutes to the two fixes that didn't work before she got to the one that did. Most conference postmortems are victory laps. Hers wasn't.

Everything else happened between sessions. Three teams, strangers to each other and to us, told the same story: they had torn out their staging environment. Not trimmed it. Deleted it, and put the money into progressive rollouts and faster rollback. The reason never varied — staging drifted from prod inside a few weeks and left everyone confidently wrong.

We are not agreed on this. Marcus calls it survivorship bias from shops with deploy tooling we don't have. Priya says he's defending a system he built. Neither has to be wrong.

Two things we're changing anyway. We're going to put a stopwatch on our rollbacks, because nobody here can tell you how long one takes, which is a poor look for a team that says "blast radius" as much as we do. And our incident reviews will start including the attempts that failed. It costs us nothing, and on the evidence of that outage talk, it's the part anyone remembers.

Notes are in the shared doc. Ask us about the vendor floor another time — that's its own post.
